transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

I... I've been feeling really anxious lately because I keep hearing these strange voices that nobody else seems to hear. On top of that, I constantly feel like I'm being watched and monitored wherever I go. I just really need some help because it won't stop.

I'm so sorry you're dealing with that. Along with these voices and feelings of being watched, have you noticed any major changes in your mood, like feeling extremely down or unusually high and energetic?

No, I haven't really noticed feeling unusually high or energetic, and I don't think I've felt extremely down either. Mostly, I'm just feeling very anxious and stressed because of the voices and the constant feeling of being watched.
Could you tell me a bit more about the voices you hear—are they clear, distinct voices talking to you or about you, and how often do they happen?

Yes, they sound like very clear, distinct voices of real people talking to me or about me, even when I'm completely alone. They happen quite frequently throughout the day, and this has been going on for about 8 months now.
How have these experiences impacted your ability to work, handle daily tasks, or maintain your relationships with others?

These experiences have severely impacted my life, and I've lost all motivation to do daily chores or focus on my work. I've also completely withdrawn from my family and friends because I no longer feel like socializing or find any pleasure in being around people.

latest_inference.note: The patient has experienced auditory hallucinations, persecutory delusions, and prominent negative symptoms (avolition, asociality) for 8 months, causing severe functional impairment. Mood disorders have been ruled out. This presentation meets the full DSM-5 criteria for Schizophrenia, so the candidate remains Schizophrenia and we can finalize the diagnosis.
